summary: The paper describes the growth of Lu2O3 thin films using atomic-layer deposition (ALD) at 370 °C with a biscyclopentadienyl-Lu compound and H2O as precursors. The films were annealed at 650 °C to induce crystallization. The study focuses on the dielectric properties of Lu2O3, analyzing its vibrational modes and comparing experimental results with first-principles calculations.
evidence: Lu2O3 films were grown by atomic-layer deposition (ALD) at a growth temperature of 370 °C. Each single growth cycle consisted of separate pulses of (i) a biscyclopentadienyl-Lu compound as a precursor of Lu (duration: 11 s); (ii) N2 for purging (8 s); (iii) H2O as O precursor (11 s); (iv) N2 to purge again (8 s).
